rule: when naming a physical mechanism, prioritize evidence closest in organ, geometry and taxonomic context; broader analogs cannot rescue a mechanism unsupported by closer evidence

orientation.geometry_restriction: vertical nodding-versus-erect capitulum manipulations prioritized over azimuthal orientation or nonhomologous flower-orientation systems
orientation.leading_physical_mechanism: protection of reproductive tissues from wetting/rain and UV-B exposure
orientation.link_to_focal_result: compatible with the focal East-Asian transition-regime signal, but BIO15/BIO1 are ecological regime coordinates rather than direct wetting/UV measurements
orientation.origin_boundary: not demonstrated as the origin cause because current regime persistence is only 99/376 scenarios

phyllary.structure_restriction: close Cardueae involucral-spine manipulation prioritized over nonhomologous bract systems; focal JPN36 natural visitor access used only as a necessity constraint
phyllary.leading_physical_mechanism: mechanical restriction of illegitimate or damaging visitor access to the reproductive head
phyllary.focal_constraint: appressed JPN36 is naturally visited by multiple bee, butterfly and hawkmoth taxa, so open/spreading phyllaries are not a demonstrated prerequisite for legitimate visitor access

stickiness.taxonomic_restriction: direct Cirsium benefit/null experiments and Cirsium arthropod-guild observations prioritized over other sticky-plant systems
stickiness.leading_physical_mechanism: guild-selective filtering of arthropod access and residence on the involucre
stickiness.net_selection_model: local arthropod-community benefit minus secretion/resistance and other trait costs

whole_capitulum.interpretation: the three traits can be functionally integrated in one capitulum while mediating different interfaces with the environment; this provides a biological mechanism-level interpretation of mosaic historical assembly
whole_capitulum.claim_boundary: distinct interface mechanisms do not prove separate genes, developmental modules, or a unique selective cause for every transition
